At first instead of the hidden menu bar appearing, I got an error message that ice can't be displayed and clicking or right-clicking on the Ice icon did nothing. On later attempts, I got the menu bar at first, then it behaved as before except without the error message. 

In both cases, I looked at the Activity Monitor which showed that Ice was not responding. I stopped it each time and tried again with the same results

Current

26.1 yesterday's beta update

comments.body: I have the same issue. Also, it's impossible to configure bar layout, because icons are missing or not visible.

> I have the same issue. Also, it's impossible to configure bar layout, because icons are missing or not visible. > > Same with me. Does it have something todo with Tahoe allowing the option for exposing apps to the menu bar?

You try with the latest beta version of ice:
https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/releases/tag/0.11.13-dev.2
The Beta you linked above is working for me on 26.0.1 whereas the official release was not.
I was having this same issue and the beta 0.11.13-dev.2 also fixed it for me.

After installing the official MacOS 26.0.1 release, Ice would crash as soon as I clicked on the icon.  The beta (0.11.13-dev.2) fixed it.  Thanks!

I see the other comments noting that the beta fixed their issues with Tahoe, but I thought it would be useful to add the detail about 11.12's behavior with MacOS 26.
That was the exact behavior I was experiencing, my bad for not elaborating and good shout @jacix
I had the same thing as jacix, installing the dev build fixed the issue for me.
Same issue here unfortunately. @raschan how did you install the dev build?

@bramn  I simply downloaded the zip file in the release that was linked above: https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/releases/tag/0.11.13-dev.2

scroll down a little, and in the `Assets` section, you will see it

I have the same bug to report. I installed `Ice` via

```
brew install --cask jordanbaird-ice
```

This didn't work. So I uninstalled it as follows:

```
brew uninstall --cask jordanbaird-ice
```

Next, I followed the [link to releases](https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/releases) and downloaded the [second beta-version (`0.11.13-dev.2`)]([Ice 0.11.13 (macOS Tahoe Beta 2)](https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/releases/tag/0.11.13-dev.2)). That does seem to work. When I click the `Ice`-icon it doesn't quit on me, and I can change the 'always hidden', 'hidden' and 'visible' icons. Seems to be the fix.

issue.title: [Bug]:  Ice App Freezes During Screen Capture Operations
issue.body:
### Search for Similar Reports

- [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports

### Description

The Ice application becomes completely unresponsive during screen capture operations. The main thread and multiple background threads are blocked indefinitely, requiring the user to force-quit the app. This issue occurs consistently when the app attempts to capture menu bar items or windows.
*(Note: I apologize for not being very familiar with Swift development, so my analysis might be limited to what I observed in the logs.)*

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Ice on macOS 26.1
2. close the ice window
4. Trigger a screen capture operation
5. Observe UI freeze and unresponsiveness
6. Check Activity Monitor or sample logs for blocked threads

### App Version

0.11.13-dev.2 

### macOS Version

26.1

### Additional Information

### Stack Trace Analysis
From the sample log, I found these key blocking points:
1. **Main thread blocked**:
   ```
   OS_dispatch_queue.sync → _dispatch_sync_f_slow → __DISPATCH_WAIT_FOR_QUEUE__ → kevent_id
   ```
2. **Screen capture queue stuck**:
   ```
   SLWindowListCreateImageFromArray → _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow → semaphore_timedwait_trap
   ```
3. **Multiple background threads blocked**:
   ```
   OS_dispatch_queue.sync (in com.apple.root.user-initiated-qos.cooperative)
   ```
### Code Location
The issue appears to be in `ScreenCapture.swift`, specifically in this method:
```swift
static func captureWindows(_ windowIDs: [CGWindowID], screenBounds: CGRect? = nil, option: CGWindowImageOption = []) -> CGImage? {
    // ... creates window array ...
    return .windowListImage(from: screenBounds ?? .null, windowArray: windowArray, imageOption: option)
}
```
This method calls `CGImage.windowListImage` which seems to be the synchronous system call causing the blockage.
### Additional Observations
- The issue is more pronounced on macOS 26.1 (Beta)
- Memory usage appears normal (75.5MB)
- The blocking occurs in the ScreenCaptureKit framework's `SLWindowListCreateImageFromArray` function

issue.title: [Bug]:Selecting 'Ice Bar' in settings and then tapping on the Ice icon causes Ice to crash
issue.body:
### Search for Similar Reports

- [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports

### Description

Hi, I'm on macOS 26.1 on two machines, a M4 Mac Mini and a M3 Pro MacBook Pro and the same thing occurs. I really like using the 'Ice Bar' in settings to have the hidden items appear in a bar under the main menubar, but since upgrading to the public release of Tahoe (26.0 - never had any of the betas) if I pull up settings, select 'Use Ice Bar' then close settings, and tap on the Ice Icon (I use the ellipsis option for the icon), it causes Ice to crash. I can restart Ice, and then go back into settings and turn Ice Bar off, and then it works fine, with hidden items appearing in the menu bar when I tap on the icon (though this is frustrating on the MacBook Pro because of the notch covering up most of my icons, hence why I used Ice Bar) and Ice not crashing. Would really like if this could be fixed if at all possible. I am running version 0.11.12, and had hoped 26.1 would fix whatever was causing the bug, but unfortunately it hasn't. Thanks Jordan! :)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Go to Settings
2. Select 'Use Ice Bar'
3. Close Settings
4. tap on Ice Icon to reveal hidden menubar items
5. Ice crashes
6. Restart Ice
7. Open Settings
8. Turn off 'Use Ice Bar'
9. Close Settings
10. Ice works

### App Version

0.11.12

### macOS Version

26.1

### Additional Information

_No response_

issue.title: Crash when enabling Ice Bar: EXC_BREAKPOINT in window handling
issue.body:
## Bug

Ice crashes when enabling "Use Ice Bar" in Settings. The app freezes, any Sparkle dialogs become unresponsive, and clicking the menu bar icon crashes the app.

## Repro

1. Open Ice Settings → General
2. Enable "Use Ice Bar"
3. Try clicking the Ice menu bar icon → crash

## Environment

- Ice 0.11.12
- macOS 26.1 (25B78), M1 Pro MacBook

## Crash Info

Exception: `EXC_BREAKPOINT` (SIGTRAP) - Swift assertion failure
Involves: `NSStatusBarWindow` / `windowNumber`
Thread: main


Looks like a race condition when the `useIceBar` setting changes - something accesses a window in an invalid state.

* **Implication:** This indicates a deliberate halt in the code execution, likely caused by a Swift runtime failure (e.g., forced unwrap of a `nil` optional, a failed assertion, or an array index out of bounds).


* **Trigger:** Thread 0 (Main / UI Thread).

**Technical Analysis:**

3. **Correlation:** The presence of `NSStatusBarWindow` in the crash registers directly correlates with the user-reported reproduction step: activating the "Ice Bar" (a secondary window/overlay for hidden items). The app likely attempted to manipulate this window reference while it was invalid or nil, triggering the trap.

Hi @xbeta — apologies for the late ping. Could I ask you to try reproducing this on a fresh build that ships with the latest macOS 26 XPC fixes?

There's a maintained fork ([pdurlej/Ice](https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice), "Fire from Ice") that ships as a signed + Apple-notarized DMG, drop-in replacement for upstream Ice (same `com.jordanbaird.Ice` bundle ID, settings carry over):

→ https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice/releases/latest

After install, please do a one-time TCC reset (the signing anchor changes when moving from upstream ad-hoc to a Developer-ID-signed build):

```sh
tccutil reset All com.jordanbaird.Ice
tccutil reset All com.jordanbaird.Ice.MenuBarItemService
osascript -e 'tell application "Ice" to quit'
open /Applications/Ice.app
# then re-grant Accessibility (and Screen Recording if used) in System Settings
```

Then try the same scenario that crashed before. **Two possible outcomes:**

1. **No more crash** → great, the fix that resolved the XPC peer-requirement regression (a different but related bug) may have addressed your issue too. Please confirm here so we can close the loop.

2. **Still crashes** → please grab the crash log from `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Ice-*.ips` (most recent file) and paste the first ~50 lines here. That gives us the stack trace + thread state we'd need to actually debug it.

Either way, your data point really helps — without crash logs from real users on real configs, these are very hard to fix in isolation. Thanks!

(Note: this is from the Fire fork maintainer, not the upstream Ice author. We're trying to triage what's already fixed vs what still needs work.)

Noice, 2 weeks old and the dudes putting in like 20 commits a day.  Looks awesome.

> There's a Beta that works fine on Tahoe

Not for everyone: it gave me problems.
Same issues. Switched the Thaw just now and it works.

The website isn't even active.

https://icemenubar.app/
Thaw works so well!  Dude responds to issues super fast and has all the fixes.

If you're looking for a lightweight alternative, I built [Glacier](https://github.com/junuMoon/Glacier) — it does the core job (hide/show/always-hidden sections) in ~200 lines of Swift with zero dependencies and no accessibility permission. Works fine on Tahoe. No settings UI though, so it's for those who just want the basics.

I understand the frustration — tools we rely on going quiet is never fun. But Ice isn't dead, it's just being continued elsewhere. I've been actively maintaining it under the name [Fire from Ice](https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice) (see [FORK.md](https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice/blob/fire/main/FORK.md) for my approach).

**fire.4 is live:** a signed + Apple-notarized DMG with full macOS 26 Tahoe support, the XPC peer-requirement fix for the blank Menu Bar Layout issue, and Sparkle auto-update so you stay current automatically going forward.

→ https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice/releases/latest

This is a continuation, not a replacement — Jordan Baird built something genuinely useful and well-designed, and I want to honor that work by keeping it running on the latest macOS. If you want to help, contributions and bug reports are always welcome at https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice/issues.

Thanks for this!

issue.title: [Bug]:
issue.body:
### Search for Similar Reports

- [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports

### Description

Immediate Crash Cause:
Ice 0.11.12 (native ARM64) triggers an EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP) exception (termination code: Trace/BPT trap: 5) on the main thread (com.apple.main-thread) under macOS 26.4 (build 25E246). The crash stack points to the Swift concurrency runtime's completeTaskWithClosure logic, caused by a main thread assertion failure when accessing the windowNumber property of NSStatusBarWindow.
Root Cause:
Ice version 0.11.12 contains a Swift concurrency thread safety defect, which is incompatible with the system menu bar UI framework of macOS 26.4 (Sequoia 15.4). A race condition is triggered when the Ice Bar feature is enabled, leading to application crash during launch or runtime.

[error.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26292858/error.txt)



### Steps to Reproduce

Click on "use ice bar"

Click the Hide button in the menu bar

See the error

### App Version

0.11.12

### macOS Version

Sequoia 15.4

### Additional Information

_No response_

Hi @Benature — apologies for the late ping. Could I ask you to try reproducing this on a fresh build that ships with the latest macOS 26 XPC fixes?

There's a maintained fork ([pdurlej/Ice](https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice), "Fire from Ice") that ships as a signed + Apple-notarized DMG, drop-in replacement for upstream Ice (same `com.jordanbaird.Ice` bundle ID, settings carry over):

→ https://github.com/pdurlej/Ice/releases/latest

After install, please do a one-time TCC reset (the signing anchor changes when moving from upstream ad-hoc to a Developer-ID-signed build):

```sh
tccutil reset All com.jordanbaird.Ice
tccutil reset All com.jordanbaird.Ice.MenuBarItemService
osascript -e 'tell application "Ice" to quit'
open /Applications/Ice.app
# then re-grant Accessibility (and Screen Recording if used) in System Settings
```

Then try the same scenario that crashed before. **Two possible outcomes:**

1. **No more crash** → great, the fix that resolved the XPC peer-requirement regression (a different but related bug) may have addressed your issue too. Please confirm here so we can close the loop.

2. **Still crashes** → please grab the crash log from `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Ice-*.ips` (most recent file) and paste the first ~50 lines here. That gives us the stack trace + thread state we'd need to actually debug it.

Either way, your data point really helps — without crash logs from real users on real configs, these are very hard to fix in isolation. Thanks!

(Note: this is from the Fire fork maintainer, not the upstream Ice author. We're trying to triage what's already fixed vs what still needs work.)

issue.title: [Bug]: crashes whenever I use the trigger button in the menu bar
issue.body:
### Search for Similar Reports

- [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports

### Description

I've set the icon to cube. Whenever I press that cube icon in the menu bar when it is not expanded, as soon as I press the cube icon, the app crashes. I have to reopen the app, and then it asks me if it can update the app automatically or it can check for updates. None of the buttons are pressable on that option pop up

### Steps to Reproduce

Open the ice app, then press the icon in the menu bar which is dedicated for the ice app expander, and then the app will fail at least it did on my MacBook Pro M5. 

### App Version

The latest one 

### macOS Version

The latest one 

### Additional Information

_No response_
